assumptions_challenged: That the supplied record contains no regulator engagement or jurisdictional precedent relevant to intranasal EV therapeutics.
That GLP large-animal intranasal biodistribution/toxicology data do not exist for this program or a suitable surrogate.
That validated potency and release assays, and representative GMP-like scale-up runs (three runs) with stability data, are absent or incomplete.
That no defined clinical indication or target population is available to map to jurisdictional pathways.
That commercial/market analyses and partner due-diligence materials needed to choose a jurisdiction are unavailable.
falsification_conditions: Provision of one or more citable regulator engagement records (pre-IND, Scientific Advice, ATMP classification, meeting minutes) that show a specific jurisdiction has accepted or provided actionable guidance for intranasal EV/MSC-EV early clinical entry; this would falsify the claim that ‘no jurisdiction-specific pathway is supported’.

Submission of GLP-compliant large-animal intranasal biodistribution and toxicology reports (or equivalent validated surrogate-data packages) demonstrating translational CNS exposure/safety; this would falsify the translational-gap assertion.

Delivery of GMP batch records from three representative scale-up runs with draft release specifications and stability datasets, plus documentation of validated/fit-for-purpose potency and orthogonal QC assays; these would falsify the CMC-readiness assertions.

Provision of a documented, regulator-aligned lead indication and target-population selection (with rationale) plus any jurisdiction-specific pathway analysis mapping that indication to an accepted regulatory route (e.g., FDA IND, EMA ATMP), which would falsify the claim that no jurisdiction can be recommended.

Provision of commercial due-diligence materials or market/reimbursement analyses linking an indication and timeline to jurisdictional feasibility, which would falsify the commercial-readiness conclusion.
strongest_objection: The reviewers’ conclusion that no jurisdiction can currently be endorsed rests on unreferenced negative claims; because no supporting or disconfirming evidence identifiers were supplied, the conclusion is unverified and may be unjustified. The record lacks any cited regulator interactions, GLP large-animal data, GMP-run documentation, validated potency/release assays, or market/regulatory precedent—so the negative determination is an evidence-free assertion rather than a substantiated finding.
